title: OpenDeepThink: Parallel Reasoning via Bradley--Terry Aggregation
description: Research paper introducing OpenDeepThink, a method for parallel reasoning using Bradley-Terry aggregation. Presents techniques for improving reasoning in AI systems through parallel processing approaches.
author: Shang Zhou, Wenhao Chai, Kaiyuan Liu, Huanzhi Mao, Qiuyang Mang, Jingbo Shang

title: APWA: A Distributed Architecture for Parallelizable Agentic Workflows
description: Presents APWA, a distributed architecture designed for parallelizable agentic workflows. Discusses approaches to scaling AI agent systems through distributed computing techniques.
author: Evan Rose, Tushin Mallick, Matthew D. Laws, Cristina Nita-Rotaru, Alina Oprea

title: Why Neighborhoods Matter: Traversal Context and Provenance in Agentic GraphRAG
description: Explores the importance of traversal context and provenance in Agentic GraphRAG systems. Submitted at IJCAI-ECAI 2026 Joint Workshop on GENAIK and NORA.
author: Riccardo Terrenzi, Maximilian von Zastrow, Serkan Ayvaz

title: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
description: Introduces Orchard, an open-source framework for agentic modeling. Provides tools and infrastructure for building sophisticated AI agent systems with advanced capabilities.
author: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Xiao Yu, Rui Yang, Tao Ge, Alessandrio Sordoni, Xingdi Yuan, Yelong Shen, Pengcheng He, Tong Zhang, Zhou Yu, Jianfeng Gao

title: Dual-Dimensional Consistency: Balancing Budget and Quality in Adaptive Inference-Time Scaling
description: Addresses the challenge of balancing computational budget with output quality in adaptive inference-time scaling for AI models. Presents techniques for optimizing the trade-off between resource usage and model performance.
author: Rongman Xu, Yifei Li, Tianzhe Zhao, Yanrui Wu, Bo Li, Hang Yan

title: Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
description: Comprehensive survey on multi-agent systems based on Large Language Models, covering collaboration patterns, failure attribution mechanisms, and self-evolution capabilities in multi-agent environments.
author: Shihao Qi, Jie Ma, Rui Xing, Wei Guo, Xiao Huang, Zhitao Gao, Jianhao Deng, Jun Liu, Lingling Zhang, Bifan Wei, Boqian Yang, Pinghui Wang, Jianwen Sun, Jing Tao, Yaqiang Wu, Hui Liu, Yu Yao, Tongliang Liu

title: GraphFlow: An Architecture for Formally Verifiable Visual Workflows Enabling Reliable Agentic AI Automation
description: Presents GraphFlow, an architecture for creating formally verifiable visual workflows for AI agent automation. Focuses on reliability and formal verification in agentic AI systems.
author: Drewry H. Morris V, Luis Valles, Reza Hosseini Ghomi

title: Case-Based Calibration of Adaptive Reasoning and Execution for LLM Tool Use
description: Introduces a case-based calibration approach for adaptive reasoning and execution when LLMs use tools. Focuses on improving how language models adaptively employ external tools.
author: Renning Pang, Tian Lan, Leyuan Liu, Piao Tong, Sheng Cao, Xiaosong Zhang

title: Holistic Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis of AI Agents
description: Presents a comprehensive framework for evaluating AI agents holistically and diagnosing failure modes. Addresses the challenge of understanding when and why AI agents fail in complex scenarios.
author: Netta Madvil, Gilad Dym, Alon Mecilati, Edo Dekel, Jonatan Liberman, Rotem Brazilay, Liron Schliesser, Max Svidlo, Shai Nir, Orel Shalom, Yaron Friedman, David Connack, Amos Rimon, Philip Tannor, Shir Chorev

title: AI Coding Impact 2026 Benchmark Report - Opsera
description: Analysis of 250,000+ developers across 60+ enterprise organizations showing AI coding adoption patterns, productivity metrics, and quality benchmarks. 84% adoption rate but only 33% trust in AI coding tools.
author: Opsera Research

title: Claude Code v2.1.142 Release - Enhanced Agent Configuration
description: Claude Code v2.1.142 brings enhanced agent configuration options with new flags like --add-dir, --settings, --mcp-config. Opus 4.7 for fast mode, and numerous stability improvements including fixed crash-loop issues with background agents.
author: Anthropic

title: AI Coding Agent Dev Tools Landscape 2026 - Reddit Discussion
description: Reddit discussion highlighting the proliferation of coding agent frameworks but noting gap in AI agents for infrastructure and incident response. Community perspectives on tooling gaps in 2026.
author: Reddit r/LLMDevs Community

title: Amjad Masad on AI Coding Impact - CEO Perspectives
description: Amjad Masad shares insights from a public company CEO who noted AI coding has had 'negligible impact' on his engineering teams, while also stating 'AI enables everyone to build apps, which leaves the best engineers to focus a layer deeper'.
author: Amjad Masad

title: 14 Best AI Coding Agents in 2026 - Comprehensive Rankings
description: Comprehensive ranking of AI coding agents by SWE-bench scores and real adoption data. Includes Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Aider, and Cline. Shows 2026 as pivotal year where AI agents went mainstream.
author: MorphLLM

title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML - Simon Willison
description: Simon Willison explores Thariq Shihipar's case for requesting HTML over Markdown from Claude. HTML enables SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, in-page navigation, and richer explanations. Willison tested this by having GPT-5.5 create an interactive HTML explanation of the copy.fail Linux exploit, demonstrating how AI-generated HTML can produce detailed, styled technical documentation with color-coded findings and structured layouts.
author: Simon Willison

title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview - Mozilla
description: Mozilla details using Claude Mythos preview to find and fix hundreds of Firefox vulnerabilities. Security bug fixes jumped from 20-30/month to 423 in April 2026. The post describes how improved model capabilities and better harnessing techniques (steering, scaling, stacking models) dramatically improved AI-generated security bug reports from 'unwanted slop' to highly valuable findings.
author: Mozilla Security Team (covered by Simon Willison)
